clue.text: Honest tone possibly about husband in front of drawing

indicators.note: in front of puts the first part ahead of the drawing word
about says the shuffled letters go round the husband's letter
possibly says the letters of tone could be arranged some other way

parts.note: teams drawing are level, neither ahead

explanation.surface: Someone's honest tone of voice, apparently, as their husband stands before a sketch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' shuffles TONE to ONTE; 'about' wraps that round H to give ONTHE. 'Drawing' is not a sketch here but a tied score.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on the level is straightforward and truthful, an idiom for honesty.

clue.text: Greasy mat daughter cleared

indicators.note: cleared means the daughter's letter is removed from the mat word

parts.note: a doily is a small decorative mat

explanation.surface: A greasy table mat that a daughter has tidied away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cleared' takes D out of DOILY.
explanation.definitionFit: Oily food or surfaces are slick with fat, a straight synonym for greasy.

clue.text: Soft material in the view of duke lacking measure of weight

parts.note: to, as in 'to me it looks fine', means in the view of

indicators.note: lacking says the weight measure is taken off the duke's title

parts.note: the Duke of Wellington, the famous British general
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A soft fabric, in the opinion of a duke who has shed a few pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes TON from WELLINGTON, leaving WELLING.
explanation.definitionFit: Towelling is the absorbent looped cotton fabric used for towels, a soft cloth.

clue.text: Wading bird, say, with others missing sun initially

parts.note: EG, for example, is signalled by say

indicators.note: missing means a letter is dropped from the word for others

parts.note: the rest means the others

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the word sun

explanation.surface: A wading bird, for instance, alone when the others have left before the sun comes up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes S from 'sun' and 'missing' drops it from REST, leaving RET.
explanation.definitionFit: An egret is a white heron that stalks through shallow water, a wading bird.

clue.text: Virginia is upset when detained by Adam's mate being equivocal

indicators.note: detained by means held inside the letters of Adam's partner

parts.note: Eve was Adam's partner in Genesis

indicators.note: upset says the letters of Virginia's abbreviation and is are tipped into a new order

parts.note: VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia, followed by is as written

explanation.surface: Virginia is annoyed at being held by Eve, who won't give a straight answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' scrambles the abbreviation plus IS to ASIV, and 'detained by' sets it inside Adam's wife. 'being' is only a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: Being evasive means dodging a clear answer, which is what equivocal speech does.

clue.text: Unlimited ambition shown by lieutenant firstly on English ship

parts.note: an end is an aim or ambition

indicators.note: firstly picks the opening letter of the word lieutenant

parts.note: SS, steamship, is the usual crossword ship

explanation.surface: A young officer's boundless ambition displayed aboard an English vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Something endless has no boundary in time or extent, so it is without limits.

clue.text: Some blouse definitely is handed down?

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A blouse that is certainly a hand-me-down from an older sister.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is loose: a hand-me-down garment has been worn before.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing passed down to a younger sibling is secondhand, already worn by someone else.

clue.text: Rod has to swagger

definitions.meaning: a bar or rod bracing a structure

explanation.definitionFit: A strut is a supporting bar, and strutting is a proud, showy walk.

clue.text: One very like another regarded in ground

indicators.note: ground, as in coffee ground up, says the letters of regarded and in are broken and remade

explanation.surface: A lookalike, admired on the football ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like a sports pitch but is the past tense of grind, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead ringer is an idiom for someone who closely resembles another person.

clue.text: Soften scowl

definitions.meaning: to ... a voice or tone is to soften it
..., also spelt lour, means to frown or scowl

explanation.definitionFit: Lowering a voice quietens it, and an old sense of lower means to look sullen and frown.

clue.text: Financial professional recalled excellent places to view performances?

parts.note: an auditor checks company accounts

indicators.note: recalled, called back, says the excellent letters run backwards

parts.note: A1 means excellent, written AI in crosswords

explanation.surface: An accountant remembers some first-rate theatres.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' reverses AI (A1, excellent) to IA.
explanation.definitionFit: Auditoria are the halls where audiences sit to watch shows, the plural of auditorium.

clue.text: Short period in school with competition in paved area by building

indicators.note: short says the school period word loses its final letter

parts.note: a term is one part of the school year
a race is a contest

explanation.surface: A brief school stint involving a contest out on the patio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' cuts the last letter from TERM, leaving TER.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrace is a flat paved space beside a house, used for sitting outdoors.

clue.text: Large storage site close to telephone network

parts.note: an attic is where things are stored under the roof

indicators.note: close to, meaning the end of, picks the final letter of telephone

explanation.surface: A big warehouse beside a phone network.
explanation.walkthrough: 'network' looks like telecoms, but means a crisscross pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: A lattice is a framework of crossed strips, a network of interlacing bars.

clue.text: Rubbish found by soldiers in part of helicopter

parts.note: rot means nonsense or rubbish
OR, other ranks, are ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Debris discovered by troops inside a helicopter.
explanation.definitionFit: The rotor is the spinning assembly of blades that lifts a helicopter.

clue.text: Group attending talks showing no aptitude for negotiation

indicators.note: for negotiation says these letters are open to being worked round into a new deal, a new order

explanation.surface: A delegation shows it has no talent for bargaining.
explanation.definitionFit: A deputation is a group of delegates sent to represent others in talks.

clue.text: Record independent book showing illustration

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: A record by an independent label, plus a book with pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'illustration' suggests pictures, but means a perfect example.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitome is a perfect example of something, so it illustrates a type.

clue.text: Inferior far too haphazard about last part of duties

indicators.note: about says the jumbled letters go round the final letter of duties
haphazard says the letters of far too are set down in random order
last part of picks the closing letter of the word duties

explanation.surface: Second-rate work, far too careless over the end of one's duties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'haphazard' shuffles FAR TOO, and 'about' puts it round S, the last letter of 'duties'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something described as 'of a sort' is a poor or second-rate example of its kind.

clue.text: Section in medical facility lacking in comfort?

indicators.note: in says the section word sits inside the medical facility word

parts.note: a san is short for sanatorium, a medical facility
a part is a section

explanation.surface: A ward within a clinic that is short on comfort.
explanation.definitionFit: Spartan living is austere and bare, after the famously hardy Spartans.

clue.text: Place to get fuel in Rome?

definitions.text: Place to get fuel in Rome?

parts.words: Place to get fuel in Rome?
parts.note: fuel suggests a petrol station, but here it is food that fuels a person, and the place is an Italian eatery

explanation.surface: Where to fill up on petrol in the Italian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fuel' means food for the body, not petrol.
explanation.definitionFit: A trattoria is a simple Italian restaurant, where diners refuel on food.

clue.text: Better qualified student is engaged in refined exercise

parts.note: U means upper-class, refined

indicators.note: is engaged in means held within the exercise letters

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercise
a grad is a graduate, a student who has qualified

explanation.surface: A more highly qualified student takes part in polished exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better qualified' looks like one phrase but splits: 'Better' is a verb. U for upper-class is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: To upgrade something is to improve it, so it is a verb meaning to better.

clue.text: Established working area around current European state

indicators.note: around says the first three pieces together go round the current symbol

parts.note: on means working, as a machine is on
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: An established working region around present-day Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' wraps the first three pieces, ESTONA, round I, the physics symbol for current.
explanation.definitionFit: Estonia is a Baltic country, a member state of the European Union.

clue.text: Look shown by mature aristocrats?

parts.note: to peer is to look closely
to age is to mature

explanation.surface: The gaze of older noblemen.
explanation.definitionFit: The peerage is the body of peers, the titled nobility of Britain.

clue.text: Pedants elevated titled figure in places

indicators.note: in says the raised letters sit inside the places word

parts.note: puts means places, as a verb

indicators.note: elevated, raised up in a down clue, says the titled figure's letters read upwards

parts.note: Sir is the title of a knight

explanation.surface: Fussy people promote a knight to a higher position.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'elevated' means read upwards, so the knight's title is reversed; 'in' then places it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Purists insist on strict correctness, as pedants do.

clue.text: A learner given a brief time noted fort

parts.note: L is for learner, as on a learner driver's plate
a mo is a moment, a brief time

explanation.surface: A trainee has been allowed a moment at a famous stronghold.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alamo, in Texas, is the mission fort famous for its 1836 siege.

clue.text: Bitter councillor blocking financial support

indicators.note: blocking says the councillor stands in the way inside the support word

parts.note: aid is help, here money

explanation.surface: An angry councillor stands in the way of a grant.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrid means sharp and pungent in taste or smell, so bitter.

clue.text: Small pastry later crumbles in transit after dropping load

indicators.note: in says the crumbled letters go inside what is left of transit
after dropping load means the inner letters of transit, its cargo, are emptied out, keeping only the ends
crumbles says the letters of later break apart and are reassembled

explanation.surface: A little tart falls to pieces in transport once the cargo is unloaded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after dropping load' empties transit, keeping just its outer Ts; 'crumbles' remakes the letters of later as ARTLE, and 'in' sets those between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A tartlet is a small tart, a little pastry case with a filling.

clue.text: Wild cat reported in seaside golf course

indicators.note: reported means as spoken, so the cat's name is heard rather than seen

parts.note: a lynx is a wild cat

explanation.surface: A wildcat sighting is reported on a coastal golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: A links is a golf course on sandy coastal land, the traditional Scottish type.

clue.text: Adjustable accessory has label touching clothing

indicators.note: clothing, covering, says the words around wrap the answer, which sits within them

explanation.surface: A buckled item carries a label next to the garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothing' looks like the garment but signals that 'label touching' clothes the answer: laBEL Touching.
explanation.definitionFit: A belt is a strap worn round the waist and fastened by notches, so its size can be changed.

clue.text: Annoying types misuse IT in arts? About right

indicators.note: About says the jumbled letters go round the right letter
misuse says the letters of IT in arts are put to the wrong use, out of order

explanation.surface: Irritating people abuse information technology in the arts, and they are about right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'IT in arts' is fodder, not an instruction to insert: 'misuse' shuffles all of it, and 'About' wraps that round R.
explanation.definitionFit: Irritants are things or people that cause annoyance, so nuisances.

clue.text: Look after uniformed worker

explanation.definitionFit: Nursing means tending the sick, and a nurse is the hospital carer who wears a uniform.

clue.text: Artistic subject in muddle at intervals

indicators.note: at intervals means taking every other letter of in muddle

explanation.surface: A painting's subject ends up in a mess, now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: A nude is a picture or sculpture of an unclothed figure, a classic subject in art.

clue.text: Female with a line ready about celebrity makes flawed beginning

indicators.note: about says the ready word goes round the celebrity word

parts.note: set means ready, as in 'ready, steady, go'
a star is a celebrity

explanation.surface: A woman with a script, ready to go around a famous actor, gets off to a bad start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' makes the ready word surround the celebrity, giving SESTART; 'with' and 'makes' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A false start is a botched opening, as when a sprinter leaves before the gun.
